Elon Musk made his fortune primarily through business ownership, not salary. He received about $22 million when Compaq bought Zip2 in 1999 and later nearly $170 million from eBay’s acquisition of PayPal. He then reinvested substantial amounts of that capital into much larger ventures, particularly SpaceX and Tesla.
As those companies became dramatically more valuable, the value of Musk’s ownership stakes rose with them.
His wealth-building path can be summarized simply:
Zip2 → PayPal → reinvestment → Tesla and SpaceX equity → massive growth in company value
The key distinction is that Zip2 and PayPal generated money Musk could reinvest. Tesla and SpaceX later created wealth on an entirely different scale through the increasing value of his ownership.
How Elon Musk Made His Money at a Glance
Stage | What Happened | Why It Mattered |
Zip2 | Musk co-founded an internet software company that Compaq bought in 1999 | Created his first multimillion-dollar payday |
X.com and PayPal | He reinvested much of his early capital into online financial services | PayPal’s sale produced a much larger financial windfall |
SpaceX | Musk founded and heavily financed the aerospace company | His retained ownership eventually became enormously valuable |
Tesla | He became a major early investor, chairman and later CEO | Tesla’s rise transformed the scale of his wealth |
Equity appreciation | Musk retained large positions as his companies grew | Rising valuations, rather than ordinary salary, drove most of his later fortune |
Zip2 Gave Elon Musk His First Major Payday
Musk’s first major financial success came from Zip2 , an internet software company he co-founded with his brother Kimbal Musk during the 1990s.
Zip2 provided internet-based business directories and city information during the early years of commercial web publishing.
In 1999, Compaq acquired the company, and Musk received approximately $22 million for his stake , according to Forbes’ account of his early business career.
That made Musk a multimillionaire, but it was only the first stage of his wealth-building journey.
The more important decision came afterward.
Instead of simply preserving the money, Musk committed a substantial portion of his new capital to another technology venture.
PayPal Turned Millions Into Much More Capital
After Zip2, Musk founded X.com , an online financial-services company.
X.com later merged with Confinity, whose payment product developed into PayPal. Musk did not remain chief executive, but he retained a substantial ownership position in the combined business.
When eBay acquired PayPal in 2002, Musk received nearly $170 million in eBay stock , according to Forbes.
That transaction was much more important than simply making him richer.
It gave Musk the financial capacity to pursue businesses that required significantly more capital than a conventional internet startup.
Zip2 created his first serious pool of capital. PayPal multiplied it.

Elon Musk Childhood and Parents: Early Life Story
Elon Musk grew up in Pretoria, South Africa, in a family shaped by divorce, technical interests and financial uncertainty. His early programming experiments and move to Canada preceded the first companies that launched his career.
Jordan Ellis August 21, 2026 · Updated August 30, 2026
In this story
Key takeaways
Elon Musk was born in Pretoria, South Africa, and grew up with siblings Kimbal and Tosca.
His parents, Maye Musk and Errol Musk, divorced when he was 10, according to Biography.com.
He taught himself programming, sold the game Blastar as a child and later co-founded Zip2 with Kimbal.
Elon Musk’s childhood began in Pretoria, South Africa, where he was raised with his brother, Kimbal, and sister, Tosca. His parents, Maye Musk and Errol Musk, divorced when he was 10, according to Biography.com’s account of Elon Musk’s early life . As a teenager, he became interested in computers, taught himself programming and sold a simple video game at age 12. Those experiences formed the earliest documented link between Musk’s childhood interests and his later technology career.
Musk was born Elon Reeve Musk on June 28, 1971, in Pretoria. The family circumstances described in available biographies are more complicated than a simple story of effortless privilege. Biography.com identifies his father, Errol Musk, as a wealthy South African engineer and says his mother, Maye Musk, worked multiple jobs—including five at one point—to support the family. These descriptions come from published biographical accounts; they do not establish every detail of the family’s finances or home life.
What Elon Musk’s parents did—and did not—determine
Maye Musk built a public career as a Canadian model and later became widely known in her own right. The supplied biographical record describes her as the oldest woman to appear in a CoverGirl campaign. Errol Musk is identified as an engineer in South Africa. Together, those details help explain the professional environment around Musk, but they do not prove that his parents directed his later business choices.
The family’s divorce was an important event in Musk’s early life. Biography.com says he spent his childhood with Kimbal and Tosca in South Africa and that his parents separated when he was 10. Public accounts differ in how they describe the years that followed, so it is safer to avoid presenting one definitive version of his household arrangements or relationship with either parent.
For readers looking for the broader timeline, the full Elon Musk profile from Newsr covers his later companies and public career. This article stays focused on the childhood, parents and early foundations that came before those ventures.
